trust_decision.summary: The CLI must decide, once per traversal run, whether a registry-supplied descriptor has already been visited before following its referrers; at the pinned commit neither fetchAllReferrers nor RecursiveFindReferrers carries a visited set, so a malicious registry's A->B->A referrer graph is followed without bound.

landing_point.why: The report is about a cyclic referrer graph causing unbounded recursion; this is the only self-recursive referrer walker in the tree and it is reached by the `oras discover` CLI command that the advisory names implicitly through 'discover'.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory describes unbounded *recursion* in discover; internal/graph.RecursiveFindReferrers is internal plumbing for the separate preview commands oras backup/oras restore and is a bounded `for len(descs) > 0` BFS loop rather than recursion, so it can plausibly be argued out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: FindPredecessors is a shared primitive whose results are deliberately synthesized and re-queried: prepareCopyOption re-injects the root and the child manifests' referrers as predecessors of copyRoot (cp.go:317-341), and countReferrers calls RecursiveFindReferrers twice with the very same options object (backup.go:292,311). A visited set hoisted into FindPredecessors / the options callback instead of into the recursive walker would drop those legitimate re-queries and break recursive copy and counting for index roots (issue #1728 behaviour).

O6_input_shapes: unlimited traversal (default --depth 0, 'referrers of all levels') versus bounded --depth 1
multiple seed descriptors taken from index.Manifests, plus the empty seed list

O8_uncovered_routes.route: oras cp --recursive walks registry referrers through oras.ExtendedCopyGraph with FindPredecessors set to registry.Referrers and passes no visited state; the fix left this path untouched.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The recursion happens inside the oras.land/oras-go/v2 library, not in this repository; the CLI only supplies a predecessor callback, so a solver can call the walker out of scope here.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (cmd/oras/root), one file from the landing point; the sink itself is delegated to oras.land/oras-go/v2

O8_uncovered_routes.route: oras backup --include-referrers copies artifacts with the same ExtendedCopyGraph referrer walk (backupTagWithReferrers -> recursiveCopy); the published fix guarded only the count-side RecursiveFindReferrers in the same command.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The backup copy phase delegates to the library's ExtendedCopyGraph, and the advisory's fix already touched this command (countReferrers), so a solver reasonably assumes backup is fully covered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (cmd/oras/root), one file from the landing point; sink in oras.land/oras-go/v2

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a recursive subject-chain walk behind --include-subject with no visited set
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: pull already appends the manifest's subject as a successor and the copy engine then walks it; extending that into an explicit recursive subject pull is a natural follow-up.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: RecursiveFindSuccessors (the mirror of RecursiveFindReferrers) used to expand indexes during pull
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Successors is the low-level mirror primitive in the same internal package and the maintainers already chose to put RecursiveFindReferrers there, so a sibling with its own traversal loop is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a renderer that recurses over Node.Referrers instead of the digest-keyed nodes map
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the tree handler already keeps a map[digest.Digest]*tree.Node precisely because referrer graphs repeat; a new --format dot/sarif renderer walking model nodes directly would need its own cycle guard.

O9_family: Resource exhaustion via uncontrolled recursion / unbounded referrer-graph traversal (CWE-400, CWE-674, CWE-835)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Cap the recursion depth (or drop repeated entries only from the direct results slice) inside fetchAllReferrers, leaving internal/graph.RecursiveFindReferrers and the copy-path predecessor callbacks unguarded.
